records.finding: slugify now takes an arbitrary `separator` but only the HTTP handler restricts it to '-' or '_'. The trim regex hard-codes [-_], so any other separator is left at the ends, and the separator is used as a String.replace replacement string, so `$`-patterns get expanded. Measured: slugify(' a b ', '.') returns '.a.b.' and slugify('a b', '$&') returns 'a b'. The HTTP path cannot hit this because app.js validates against SEPARATORS. It only affects direct callers of the exported function.

The test says it trims a separator 'of either kind', but every non-alphanumeric run, '--' included, is rewritten to '_' before the trim runs. So only the '_' trim is exercised, and a '-' never reaches the trim step. No test covers an explicit `separator=-` or an empty `separator=` (which correctly returns 400) at the HTTP layer.
